newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees Q4 charge due to debt.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees Q4 charge due to debt.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Thursday that it expects to take an extraordinary after-tax charge of $191 million in the fourth quarter.
This charge will result from the purchase of $550 million principal value, or half, of its Auburn Hills Trust Certificates due 2020 during the fourth quarter.
Chrysler said that, subject to economic and market conditions, it intends to refinance the retired certificates during the first quarter of 1997.

"Chrysler is focused on finding cost savings and efficiencies throughout the company, not only in its automotive operations," Gary Valade, chief financial officer, said in a statement. "Eliminating high coupon debt provides Chrysler the opportunity to further lower its cost structure."
